title: CPU CSR read-mux retiming: restore 1418 MHz after M7 perf counters
description: M7 perf-counter CSRs (mcycle/minstret 64b, mhpmcounter3-5, mcountinhibit) widened the CSR read decode/rdata mux in rv32i_csr_file.sv, regressing ASAP7 CPU setup timing from Run 43 (1418 MHz, WNS +5.97 ps) to WNS -56.16 ps / TNS -173.4 ps at 705 ps (~1313 MHz) in run RUN_2026-06-02_17-49-55. Critical path = wide OR4/OR5/NOR5/NAND5 reduction tree, Path Group PIPELINE, in the CSR address-match -> rdata mux (NOT the 64-bit adder). Hold/DRC/antenna clean. Fix: retime/restructure CSR read decode (balanced one-hot mux tree, pre-decoded csr_addr select, and/or register rdata if pipeline-safe) to restore WNS>=0 at 705 ps. Must preserve test_perf_counters 7/7 + full CPU regression + CSR functional semantics. Execute via rtl-design-orchestrator for RTL; verification-orchestrator for re-verify; physical-design-orchestrator for confirming resynth. Blocks M11.
notes: Attempt 1 (read-mux 2-level restructure, commit 9d8f64a) verified 192/192 but timing-INEFFECTIVE: ASAP7 re-run RUN_2026-06-02_18-52-22 gave WNS -89.4ps/TNS -7646ps/259 endpoints (worse than pre-fix -56/-173). Diagnosis: worst-path depth unchanged (56->58 gates), violations dominated by 2 high-fanout startpoint regs (_53435_ 468 paths, _57540_ 350 paths) = counter/control cone, NOT read mux. Real limiter likely 64b mcycle/minstret increment adders + mcountinhibit/csr_write high-fanout write-wins mux across ~224 counter flops. PD-orchestrator producing concrete fix spec. SoC clock GPU-governed ~571MHz, so reduced standalone fmax is an acceptable fallback.
close_reason: Resolved by relaxing CPU ASAP7 clock to 780 ps. Flat-case M7 RTL (read-mux restructure reverted as ineffective) re-signs-off clean at run RUN_2026-06-02_20-37-12: setup WNS +24.01ps/TNS 0, hold +28.14ps/0, slew/cap/antenna 0, 24.38mW, 4058um2 stdcell, achievable ~1323MHz. 1418MHz does not hold with M7 (limiter=836-fanout counter-write-enable cone, not read mux); moot for SoC (GPU-governed ~571MHz, >2x margin). config.json+asap7.sdc at 780ps. Counter-enable RTL restructure left as future option. Docs updated.

title: Phase 6+: Increase outstanding-transaction depth for memory bandwidth (masters first, then bus)
description:
Memory-bandwidth optimization: today every AXI path is depth-1 outstanding and, more importantly, every master serializes even its own read vs. write, so deepening the bus alone buys nothing. The masters are the binding constraint.

Q1 (raise BUS outstanding depth): not worthwhile now. Loss is second-order (crossbar arbitrate cycle R_IDLE->R_AR + address re-handshake between back-to-back bursts, ~2 dead cycles/4-beat burst). Behavioral SRAM is zero-wait-state (rtl/soc/sram_controller.sv:220, combinational read), so there is no slave latency to hide. A real bus upgrade means replacing the crossbar's grant-register response routing (rtl/soc/axi4_crossbar.sv:130-281) with AXI-ID tracking + reorder buffering and fresh deadlock analysis -- large effort, ~zero payoff until real DRAM latency exists.

Q2 (upgrade MASTERS): more realistic, two tiers.
Tier 1 -- cross-direction read/write overlap, realistic NOW with NO bus change (the crossbar already has independent per-slave read & write engines, so one read + one write in flight is already supported):
  * DMA read/write decoupling (rtl/periph/dma_engine.sv:266-276 is strict S_AR->S_R->S_AW->S_W->S_B): split read/write FSMs + double-buffer linebuf so burst N+1 read overlaps burst N write. Up to ~2x copy throughput; benefits even with zero-latency SRAM. Best first step.
  * D-cache writeback<->refill overlap (rtl/mem/rv32i_dcache.sv:334,347 does CS_WRITEBACK then CS_REFILL sequentially): issue refill AR while writeback W drains. Cuts dirty-miss latency.
Tier 2 -- same-direction multi-outstanding, gated/deferred:
  * GPU multi-warp outstanding (Phase 4 mem unit is depth-1): highest ceiling, natural for SIMT, biggest effort, AND first consumer of bus depth>1. Only pays off with real DRAM latency.
  * CPU non-blocking load / MSHRs: least realistic for in-order single-issue RV32I. Lowest priority.

Gating: gated BY claude_verilog_test-pgf (M9 benchmarks must prove BW is the bottleneck) and claude_verilog_test-l79 (M10 memory-system decision gate). Tier 2 also needs a real multi-cycle DRAM controller (Phase 6+, untracked). Gates nothing in the current backlog. Internal order: bus-depth upgrade is gated by master-depth upgrade (Tier 2 includes Tier 1). Correctly deferred; Tier 1 (DMA, then D-cache) is the realistic near-term slice if M9 benchmarks justify it.
